rationales: Mustard is a multicellular plant, not a colonial organism.
A frog is a multicellular animal, not a colony.
Amoeba is a unicellular organism that lives independently.
Volvox consists of cells organized into a colony.
The renal artery carries oxygenated blood to the kidneys.
The aorta carries oxygenated blood from the heart to the body.
The pulmonary vein carries oxygenated blood from the lungs to the heart.
The pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood from the heart to the lungs.
Glucose is broken down during glycolysis before its products enter cellular respiration pathways.
Pyruvic acid is converted to acetyl Co-A before entering the Krebs cycle.
Citric acid is produced within the Krebs cycle rather than entering it as the starting molecule.
Acetyl Co-A enters the Krebs cycle by combining with oxaloacetate.
Emulsification breaks large lipid droplets into smaller droplets.
Absorption is the uptake of digested nutrients into the body.
Peristalsis moves food through the digestive tract.
Digestion is the broader breakdown of food and does not specifically name the dispersal of lipid droplets.
Arteries generally do not have valves along their lengths to prevent backflow.
Veins contain valves that help prevent the backward flow of blood.
Capillaries do not contain valves.
Not all three vessel types have valves to prevent backflow.
The pericycle is a root tissue and does not contain guard cells.
Guard cells surround the stomatal pore and regulate its opening.
The cortex is not where guard cells are found.
The endodermis is a root tissue and does not contain guard cells.
ATP is commonly described as having three components: adenine, ribose, and a chain of three phosphate groups.
Four is not the number of main components used in this description of ATP.
ATP has more than one component.
Two is not the number of main components used in this description of ATP.
Viruses are not classified in the kingdom Monera.
Viruses are not classified in the kingdom Protista.
Viruses are not classified in the kingdom Fungi.
Viruses are generally not assigned to any of the kingdoms because they are acellular.
Fungi generally have cell walls made mainly of chitin.
Algae generally have cell walls.
Prokaryotes generally have cell walls, although there are exceptions such as some bacteria.
Protozoans lack cell walls.
Trypsin works best in an alkaline medium, such as that in the small intestine.
An acidic medium is not optimal for trypsin.
A neutral medium is not the optimal condition for trypsin.
Strongly acidic conditions are unsuitable for trypsin.
Meiosis produces gametes and is not the process that regenerates an arm.
Budding is not the usual process by which a sea star regrows a lost arm.
Mitosis produces new body cells needed for regeneration.
Binary fission is a form of reproduction in some unicellular organisms, not arm regeneration in sea stars.
Ribosomes synthesize proteins.
Ribosomes do not synthesize RNA as their primary function.
Ribosomes do not synthesize DNA.
Ribosomes do not synthesize glucose.
Morphology studies the form and external structure of organisms.
Anatomy studies the structure of organisms and their parts, not specifically the microscopic study of tissues.
Histology is the microscopic study of tissues.
Physiology studies how organisms and their parts function.
Glucose is a small molecule and is classified as a micromolecule.
Lipids are generally classified as macromolecules in this context.
Proteins are macromolecules.
Starch is a polysaccharide and therefore a macromolecule.
A hypothesis is a tentative explanation, not an irrefutable scientific principle.
A deduction is a conclusion drawn from premises or evidence.
An experiment is a procedure for testing an idea, not a scientific principle.
A theory is the intended option for an established scientific explanation, though scientific theories are evidence-based rather than literally irrefutable.
